commands.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_counters
commands.purpose: Read the WiFi SDIO command, transfer, timeout and error counters without clearing them.
commands.review_evidence: A0454F76 checks card availability, calls vtable +0x14 with port 0 and a 40-byte stack buffer, and prints only on interface result 1. Resolved A03C0882 -> A03C67C0 -> A03C129A copies ten words from driver object +0x3c4 into that buffer; no counter reset or card transaction.
commands.side_effects_assessment: Cached RAM reads, stack writes and UART output. Counters remain untouched by the getter.

commands.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_caps
commands.purpose: Read the SDIO manufacturer/device IDs, function capabilities, block sizes, and speed support needed by the emulator.
commands.review_evidence: A0454796 sends request 0x65 into a 0xac-byte stack structure, then request 0x64 into the same request output. Resolved A03C668E queues to A03C69C4; 0x65 selects A03C6D14, which copies cached CCCR/FBR and manufacturer/device fields via A03C130E/A03C1322/A03C12D6; 0x64 selects A03C6A66, which copies cached function count and function sizes via A03C138E/A03C13A0/A03C13A4. Formatting runs only after successful request completion.
commands.side_effects_assessment: Two serialized driver requests, semaphore/queue bookkeeping, cached RAM reads, caller-buffer writes and UART output. These selectors do not issue discovery, configuration, radio connection, reset or nonvolatile writes.
commands.result_limitations: The helper waits for request completion internally; host timeout is a capture bound, not a guarantee that every firmware fault is bounded. These fields are cached capability values, not a new card enumeration.

commands.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_status
commands.purpose: Read and dump the current 32 bytes at SDIO function 0 offsets 0x00..0x1f.
commands.review_evidence: A04546C4 -> resolved vtable +0x20 A03C08A2 -> A03C6816 -> A03C4BD8. Last helper invokes A03C506C with direction 0, function 0, address 0, length 0x20 and a stack output buffer. A03C52E4 loops over exactly 32 bytes using A03C13DC. A045EE36 prints the successful read as hex.
commands.side_effects_assessment: 32 SDIO read transactions and normal controller/request bookkeeping; this will increment the SDIO counters. No write request to card configuration, connection, scan, or persistent settings is selected.
commands.result_limitations: CCCR registers are live, so compare to the cached capability dump without assuming atomicity. Handler success alone is weak: A03C6816 returns 1 after its helper even if that helper prints a read failure; require the 32-byte dump.

commands.name: ultra_spectra.get_iovar
commands.purpose: Read the WiFi driver integer variable mpc.
commands.review_evidence: A0453F3A consumes one bounded string (100-byte input buffer). A0459322 checks the driver pointer, calls A0459414 with no input payload and 4-byte output, and prints only on success. A0459414 passes ioctl 0x106 through getter A0459568 (vtable +0x0c), while setters use 0x107 through A045955C. The selected variable names occur in this firmware: mpc at A04585B8, nmode at A062303C. The corresponding getter output is interpreted as a little-endian 32-bit integer by A0459656.
commands.side_effects_assessment: A driver GET_VAR request with a variable name only, stack buffers, transaction bookkeeping and UART output. No setter payload or nonvolatile configuration path is selected.
commands.result_limitations: The radio firmware can reject unsupported variables. An empty result with a normal prompt is not a successful value read. Do not use this integer handler for strings such as ver or for secret material.

commands.name: ultra_spectra.test_endian
commands.purpose: Record the compiled 16/32/64-bit endian conversion test vectors for emulator comparison.
commands.review_evidence: A045520A..A045527E prints twelve literal vectors through A0453EEE and returns; all values are fixed immediates/literals (0x0102, 0x01020304, 0x0102030405060708 and their reversed-byte counterparts). There is no hardware access.
commands.side_effects_assessment: UART output and stack/formatting bookkeeping only.
commands.result_limitations: These are compiled fixed-vector outputs. They are not evidence that the physical SDIO bus exercised all endian cases.

commands.name: webfwupdate.get_base_md
commands.purpose: Read the 16-byte base firmware digest and any matching base_md entry in local secure configuration.
commands.review_evidence: A0470EEA reads 16 bytes from the existing base-MD pointer at 20E09780 and formats 32 hex characters via A046ED8A. It then requests section web_product_update/key base_md with a 65-byte output buffer through A03C8882/A03C8696. The secure-configuration helper seeks and reads existing cached file descriptors; it never selects a file write. Missing entry is skipped because caller passed a NULL default.
commands.side_effects_assessment: Local metadata reads and UART output. Secure-config lookup uses its mutex and changes file positions; on bad/stale file reads it can close those cached handles and compact the in-memory descriptor list. No firmware update, download, or nonvolatile write.
commands.result_limitations: The base digest pointer is initialized by the firmware lifecycle; unlike the formatted optional configuration entry it is not null-checked by this handler. Established running firmware is the precondition. This command does not recompute the digest.
